summary: Rate-cap fallback loop causing uniform 5xx saturation across streaming and embed routes
description:
Issue summary: Customers observed a broad increase in 5xx responses across streaming chat and bulk embedding routes starting 2026-03-14 09:02 UTC. The errors appeared uniform (502/503/504) and correlated with a surge in failed handshakes and repeated fallback routing to a single runtime pool. Impact: Multiple enterprise/dedicated tenants reported failed requests and long tail retries. ClearNote Health reported 25% request failure rate for embedding uploads and persistent streaming disconnects. Environment: Production (us-east), dedicated capacity cluster for several enterprise tenants. Observed at ~09:02 UTC after a minor config rollout to the edge throttler.

Immediate business impact: customer-facing functionality degraded; resumed but unreliable embeddings and chat streaming for several customers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send parallel streaming chat sessions (keepalive) and concurrent bulk embedding uploads from a dedicated tenant with concurrency ~1500 requests/s
2) Observe edge rate-limiter metrics and configured fallback rules during a throttler policy application
3) Note routing behavior when rate limits are hit: whether requests are laddered to fallback-route pool or fail fast
4) Watch runtime pods for crashloops and OOM events and API gateway 502/503/504 counts
logs: [09:02:14Z] apigw-edge: throttle-eval tenant=clearnote ratecap=500 -> exceeded, applying fallback-route multiplier=10
[09:02:15Z] router: forwarding to runtime-pool=fast-variant-4 (fallback) tenant=clearnote conn_id=abc123
[09:02:16Z] runtime-1 redwood-worker[pid=2319]: OOMKilled signal received; eviction triggered; restart
[09:03:01Z] metrics: runtime-pool fast-variant-4 error_rate=0.41 concurrent=1024 mem_free=120MB goroutine=2048
hypothesis: Edge throttler rollout introduced a fallback multiplier misconfiguration that amplifies fallback fanout (multiplier x10). When tenants briefly exceed their soft cap, requests were routed en masse to a smaller 'fallback' runtime pool with lower concurrency headroom causing OOMs and crashloops. Client retries plus hedged requests amplified load, creating a self-sustaining 5xx wave.
investigation_notes: 09:20 UTC - Confirmed spike aligns with throttler policy rollout at 09:01 UTC on edge cluster A
09:27 UTC - Observed fallback-route multiplier was set to 10 for several tenants due to a template regression in edge-config -> policy v2.3.4
09:35 UTC - fast-variant-4 runtime pool has lower GPU memory per replica (6GB) vs expected 12GB; mismatch between route metadata and runtime sizing
09:50 UTC - Client SDK retries (default backoff 100ms, 3 retries) caused amplified replays; observed repeated connection attempts in 4xx->5xx transition window
10:05 UTC - Cross-checked with dedicated-ops: autoscaler did not scale fast enough because fallback pool uses a different autoscaling policy (min_replicas=2, scale_step=1) leading to scale lag
comments: 2026-03-14T09:12Z - Support (Aisha P): Customer ClearNote Health reported embedding uploads failing with 502. Collected request IDs and initial logs; escalating to SRE.

2026-03-14T09:21Z - SRE (Liam O): Noted edge-config rollout at 09:01. Investigating fallback routing behavior and runtime pool sizing. Temporarily disabled aggressive fallback multiplier for affected tenants.
2026-03-14T09:33Z - Customer (ClearNote Health): Thanks — we see partial recovery but some streams still drop. Are you able to identify why fallback would be smaller capacity?
2026-03-14T09:38Z - Platform Eng (R. Nguyen): There was a template mismatch between route metadata and runtime selection logic introduced in PR #4582. Rolling back to previous template now.

2026-03-14T10:07Z - SRE (Liam O): Applied interim mitigation: set fallback multiplier=1 for affected tenants; increased fast-variant-4 min_replicas to 6 to absorb immediate backlog. Monitoring error rate and memory pressure.

2026-03-14T11:00Z - Support (Aisha P): Customer confirms embedding upload success rate improved to 98%; streaming disconnects reduced but some elevated latency persists. Leaving ticket open for follow-up action items.
resolution: Interim mitigation applied: rollback of edge-config template and disabled fallback multiplier amplification. Increased min_replicas on fallback runtime pool. Recommended permanent fixes: 1) Fix template parsing in edge-config PR #4582, 2) Add validation to prevent fallback multiplier > 3 for dedicated tenants unless explicit opt-in, 3) Align autoscaler policies across runtime variants, 4) Backoff-tune customer SDK guidance to reduce retry amplification.
follow_up_actions: Create bugfix PR to edge-config to validate multiplier range and route metadata -> assigned to @r_nguyen (GH PR 4589)
Run chaos test simulating soft-cap exceed to validate fallback behavior in staging
Update runbook: include steps for emergency fallback multiplier disable and scaling override
Schedule post-incident review with ClearNote Health for 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC
